reviewer1.comment: This is a really interesting and timely piece. I have a few comments which can be easily addressed via revision. Also, I did notice that you used the RAG abbreviation in the abstract, while it was only defined later in the text. Please fix this.

reviewer2_general.comment: The topic suits the journal, and the authors deserve credit for releasing per-question outputs, prompts and judge rationales; those files made it possible to check the reported results. Several of those checks do not support how the manuscript describes its own evaluation design. The main issues are: repair sets that overlap the held-out set; prospective-test items that reappear in the calibration set; a revoked regulation used as gold truth; several refusal failures that are labeling errors; and no human verification of the automated judge

comments.response: We relabel reused repair and calibration questions as development data, retain revoked-source exposure, and separate answerability adjudications from original scores. Current-law rebuilding and reevaluation and independent external validation remain incomplete; workflow benefit was outside this technical evaluation.

comments.verbatim_text: There are no baselines or ablations, so the reader cannot tell what each component contributes. Useful comparisons: BM25 alone; dense retrieval alone; with and without the reranker and anchors; a no-retrieval LLM baseline; and ideally keyword search in AnvisaLegis. This matters because all-MiniLM-L6-v2 was trained on English but is used here on Portuguese text; BM25 and the multilingual reranker may be doing most of the work. comments.response: Supplementary Section S5 provides component ablations on development questions. The separate common-prompt comparison now includes the same Gemini model with hybrid passages, BM25 passages or no retrieval. Coauthor assessment yields 19/20, 18/20 and 4/20 successful bilingual pairs, respectively. The matched lexical retrieval comparison controls the archived corpus, saved translated queries, named-regulation filtering, five seed chunks and article-completion policy; expanded context sizes vary. BM25 answer generation is sequential and reuses saved hybrid comparators. The hybrid-minus-BM25 pair difference is +5 percentage points (descriptive 95% interval -10 to +20; exact p = 1.000), without established superiority or equivalence. The English encoder was not replaced by a multilingual model. Web-search superiority and professional workflow benefit were outside this technical comparison.

comments.verbatim_text: The AI judge is not independent enough to carry the conclusions. It is the same model alias as the answer model. Its evidence was 'reconstructed from saved retrieval and rerank queries where available' (Supplementary Data S2), so it may not have seen the context the answer model saw. Faithfulness is 1.000 on every answerable row in S4 through S6, which suggests the metric is not discriminating. I recognize an expert panel was not available, but the second author has regulatory expertise. A blinded human review of a stratified sample would substantially strengthen the paper: all refusal cases, all rows below 0.8, and a random set of passes, with agreement against the judge reported. A second AI judge from a different model family would also help.
comments.response: We retain the distinct human-review layers in S3, S6 and S8 and completed coauthor review of the new common-prompt and BM25 comparisons in S10. Howard personally drafted and approved 118 distinct ratings covering all 120 condition records on 2 November 2026. He reports no exposure to AI scores, the condition key or prior findings for these outputs before finalizing, but had prior project/question exposure and answer style could reveal conditions. Original provenance fields were clarified by the corresponding author and preserved unchanged. Human and AI primary labels agree on 117/118 distinct answers; one accepted model-only answer changes its answer count from 8/40 to 9/40, not pair success. Secondary disagreements remain separately reported. This coauthor assessment is not independent external validation, not a cross-family rescoring of the historical 404 outputs, and not full human verification of the separate 300-output window-pooling experiment. Historical faithfulness saturation, unresolved backend versions and reconstructed-evidence limits remain explicit.
comments.location: Revised clean manuscript, lines 133 to 137; 153 to 179; 209 to 232; 250 to 255; 293 to 299; 322 to 351; 385 to 392. Supplementary Sections S3, S6 and S10.
